title: Using Chinese AI Models
answer: Open weight models from Chinese developers are capable and cheap, but hosted versions raise data transfer and privacy concerns, European data protection authorities have opened investigations, and US legislation has been proposed to bar such apps from government devices. Running open weights on your own infrastructure removes the data transfer issue but not every security question.

crumbs.name: AI Adoption and Governance in Life Sciences

reading.body:
Open weight Chinese models are cheap and capable, but hosted access raises data transfer and privacy problems that self hosting avoids.

The pattern is a split between the model and the service around it. The weights can be downloaded and run on your own infrastructure, which removes the data transfer question. The hosted version sends your inputs to someone else's servers, which is where European data protection authorities have opened investigations and where proposed US legislation would bar the apps from government devices. Capability and cost are not the contested ground. Custody of the data is.

For life sciences this matters more than for most sectors, because the inputs are regulated and confidential by default. The practical line the data supports is narrow and clear: no regulated or confidential data to a hosted service without a data processing agreement, and self hosted open weights evaluated by your security team. Self hosting removes the transfer issue. It does not answer every security question, and the data does not claim it does.

What the data does not cover is the outcome of any investigation, the fate of the proposed legislation, or any benchmark comparing these models to alternatives. It names no vendor beyond DeepSeek and gives no cost figures. Treat it as a map of the legal and security questions, not as an assessment of the models themselves.

siblings.name: Governing AI in a Regulated Company

explainer:
Several Chinese developers release capable open weight models, which anyone can download and run, as well as hosted chatbot and API services. Hosted services raise questions about where data are processed, which laws apply, and how prompts and outputs are retained, and some governments and regulators have restricted or investigated them.

Open weights run on a company's own infrastructure avoid sending data abroad, but security teams still assess them, for example for hidden behaviours, licence terms and the supply chain of the files. Regulated data should go only to services under appropriate contracts and data processing agreements, whatever the model's origin.
